rv.q: Cherry Jones brings her considerable star power and formidable acting skills to bear on the title role of Shaw's 1893 play, but even she can't bring this old warhorse back to life.
This production feels like a polite drawing-room exercise, when it should crackle with the heat of moral and social indignation.
But overall, a little nipping and tucking better blocked scenes, some trims of long-winded passages, warmer sets would have made this show's oftentimes arduous work a lot more appealing.
Ultimately, her accent undermines the entire enterprise and makes the revered actress’ return to the stage after several years a let-down.
With so little going on, too many of the scenes feel endless.
